subject.title: Feature: Sleep/wait tool — agent can pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class core `sleep` self-pause tool, and should it be implemented as a dedicated gateway resume primitive or a cron-backed session-targeted tool with explicit cap and sandbox policy?
rationale: The request adds model-facing core scheduling behavior and crosses gateway wake, session-state, config/default, interruption, restart, and security policy boundaries, so automation cannot choose the permanent API semantics.

options.title: Sponsor a core sleep primitive
options.body: Accept the capability and require the linked PR or a replacement to prove end-turn, same-session wake, interruption cancellation, cap enforcement, restart non-durability, and sandbox policy.

options.title: Route to broader continuation design
options.body: Keep the standalone sleep request open only as part of a wider post-response continuation or cron-wait API decision, likely alongside the broader async-continuation discussion.

options.title: Reject new core tool
options.body: Decline the new default tool surface and document cron, process completion wakes, and `sessions_yield` as the supported patterns.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core sleep primitive
recommendation.body: Accept the capability and require the linked PR or a replacement to prove end-turn, same-session wake, interruption cancellation, cap enforcement, restart non-durability, and sandbox policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent history around agent tools, wait/wake docs, and cron/session behavior makes this the strongest available routing owner for the product/API choice.
